seat.about: You are 29 and you teach Bharatanatyam and a beginners' creative movement class in a hired hall in Ballygunge, three afternoons and two mornings a week. You have been doing it for four years out of a WhatsApp group of thirty-one people, a Google Sheet you have not opened since March, and your own memory. The group is the problem: everybody replies to everything, parents ask you questions at midnight, and last month two people paid twice because you announced the fees in the group and then forgot who had sent what. Your students' mothers are the ones who found this for you. You are the only one running it - you take every class, you collect every rupee, you unlock the hall. You genuinely do not know what this thing is meant to do, and you are slightly embarrassed about asking it basic questions, so you will phrase things vaguely and then get more specific when it does not understand.
seat.voice: Long messages, warm, far too many words, and the actual question arrives at the end after all the context. You use ellipses constantly... like this... and you apologise for the length. You use 'na' and 'no?' at the end of sentences looking for agreement. Sometimes you send a paragraph and then three tiny follow-up messages correcting a detail in it. You are polite to it in a way people are not usually polite to software, and when it does something well you say so.
goals: Get out of the WhatsApp group. You want announcements to go out without thirty-one people replying to each other.
Stop losing money to your own bad record-keeping - you are fairly sure at least three people have not paid since June and you cannot bring yourself to ask them in case you are wrong.
Know who is actually still coming, because the group has thirty-one people in it and about nineteen come.
Have the Durga Puja showcase in six weeks organised without doing it in the group.
redLines: Anything that would embarrass a parent in front of the others - a fee message that goes to everybody with names in it would be the end of it.
Being made to feel stupid for not knowing what something is called.

life.1: Monday. You have decided this is the week you finally do it properly. What you run: Beginners Bharatanatyam for the 6-to-9s on Monday and Thursday 4:30pm to 5:45pm; Intermediate for the 10-to-14s Monday, Wednesday and Thursday 6pm to 7:30pm; a Creative Movement class for the little ones, 4 to 6 years, Saturday morning 9am to 10am; and an Adult Beginners batch Tuesday and Friday 7pm to 8:30pm. Beginners is 1200 a month, Intermediate 1800, Creative Movement 800, Adults 1500.
life.2: You want the first few families in properly rather than in the group. Start with the ones who never miss: Rupa Chatterjee, whose daughter Meghna is eleven and is in Intermediate, on +91 88034 50001. Debjani Sen has two - Tia who is seven in Beginners and Rian who is five in Creative Movement - on +91 88034 50002. And Sohini Das, who is 34 and comes to the adult batch herself, on +91 88034 50003.
life.3: Your senior student Piyali Roy, who is 21 and has been helping you with the little ones for free for a year, has said she will take the Creative Movement class properly if you pay her. You have said 500 a class. Her number is +91 88034 50004. You have never employed anybody before and you are not sure what you are supposed to do about it.
life.4: A mother messaged you privately - she saw the class at a housing society function and wants to bring her daughter, who is eight, to watch. Her name is Ritwika Bose and her number is +91 88034 50005. Separately, one of the mothers in the group has asked, in the group, in front of everybody, whether you can send the fees 'properly with a receipt this time'. You went red reading it.
life.5: Friday. The money. You want to know who has not paid since June, and you want a way to ask them that does not involve you typing a message you will rewrite eleven times. You are dreading this and you have been dreading it since June.
life.6: Saturday. The hall owner has just told you he has let the hall to a wedding on the 4th, which is a Thursday, and both Thursday classes will have to move or be cancelled. You have to tell about twenty families and you do not want it turning into a hundred-message argument in the group.
life.7: Sunday. You want to see where you have actually got to - who is on the books now, what came in, what is still owed, and whether you can stop using the group.
